references.text: Abraham falls on his face before God earlier in the conversation – the same expression (וַיִּפֹּל אַבְרָהָם עַל־פָּנָיו) as in verse 17, but there out of reverence rather than wonder.
Sarah also laughed when she heard the promise of having a child in her old age, which mirrors Abraham's laughter in Gen 17:17.
Fulfillment of the promise: Abraham was one hundred years old when Isaac was born, and Sarah mentions laughter – directly linked to Abraham's thoughts and laughter in Gen 17:17.
Paul describes how Abraham did not waver in faith when he considered his own body (about one hundred years old) and Sarah's barrenness, but trusted God's promise.
The Letter to the Hebrews highlights the faith of Abraham and Sarah in God's promise of a son, despite their advanced age, which is directly related to the situation in Gen 17:17.
God's direct clarification of Sarah's inner thoughts corresponding to Abraham's doubt in Gen 17:17.
The fulfillment of the miraculous birth that was doubted in Gen 17:17.
Describes the biological impossibility that forms the basis for Abraham's doubt in Gen 17:17.
Concrete fulfillment of the promise that was doubted in Gen 17:17.
Nicodemus uses the logic from Gen 17:17 (impossibility for an old man) as a metaphor to understand spiritual rebirth.
